recommended_reasoning.reason: One method's ordering inside a frozen clause, with the failure path named and its test missing. The judgement is in the partial-write question, which the packet asks to be answered explicitly.

requirements: AGENTS.md fail-closed law: when the audit cannot be written, the safe outcome is no retrieval, not an unrecorded one.
Do not catch and swallow an audit failure to keep the happy path green. An audit that fails silently is worse than one that is absent, because the absence is visible.
The IoFailure message already carries an exception string. Do not widen that pattern: a new failure member carries a class, not a message built from an exception.
risks: Writing to a temporary path and moving it into place after the audit is the obvious shape, and it is only correct if the move is atomic on the target filesystem. If that is the chosen shape, say what makes the move atomic.
Auditing before the write and rolling the audit back on failure trades one unrecorded retrieval for one recorded retrieval that did not happen. Say which of the two the chosen design prefers and why.

in: Make the retrieval fail closed on its audit: no plaintext reaches the destination unless the retrieval has been recorded, and an audit write that fails leaves no artefact behind.

Decide and state how a partially written destination is handled if the audit fails after bytes have started moving. Leaving a partial plaintext file on disk with no audit row is the same defect in a smaller form.
A test for the audit-write-failure path. Its absence is why this shipped: the existing test covers success only.
Extend the result vocabulary only if the new failure genuinely has no existing member. Say in the pull request which member it uses and why.
out: Changing the reason, role or manifest checks that precede the write. They are correct.
Changing what is audited, or the audit action name.
Adding a retrieval route, or changing who may retrieve.
